name: Turmeric and curcumin
short: Case series link turmeric supplements to liver injury, sometimes severe. Curcumin may alter levels of some drugs, including anticoagulants, mostly in non-clinical studies.
text: Case series describe liver injury after turmeric supplements: the US Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network found 10 cases, typically hepatocellular, appearing 1 to 4 months after starting, with five hospitalised and one death from acute liver failure, and an Italian series of 7 cases involved high-bioavailability, high-dose curcumin products. A review of interactions reports that curcumin can change blood levels of drugs including cardiovascular drugs, antidepressants, anticoagulants, antibiotics and chemotherapy agents, mainly by inhibiting CYP enzymes and P-glycoprotein; this evidence comes mostly from in vitro and in vivo studies, with only one clinical trial.

quotes: Ten cases of turmeric-associated liver injury were found
Five patients were hospitalized, and 1 patient died of acute liver failure.
Turmeric causes potentially severe liver injury that is typically hepatocellular, with a latency of 1 to 4 months
citations.label: Halegoua-DeMarzio et al., 2023, Am J Med
citations.title: Liver Injury Associated with Turmeric-A Growing Problem: Ten Cases from the Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network [DILIN].

quotes: Seven cases of acute hepatitis occurring in Tuscany up to September 2019 are described. In all cases, hepatotoxicity was associated with Curcuma longa formulations with high bioavailability and high dosage of curcumin/curcuminoids.
citations.label: Lombardi et al., 2021, Br J Clin Pharmacol
citations.title: Acute liver injury following turmeric use in Tuscany: An analysis of the Italian Phytovigilance database and systematic review of case reports.

quotes: Curcumin can induce pharmacokinetic alterations such as changes in Cmax and AUC when concomitantly used with pharmacological agents like cardiovascular drugs, antidepressants, anticoagulants, antibiotics, chemotherapeutic agents, and antihistamines.
The underlying mechanisms of these interactions include inhibition of cytochrome (CYP) isoenzymes and P-glycoprotein.
There is only one clinical trial which proved a significant alteration of conventional drugs in concomitant use with curcumin
Although in vitro and in vivo studies do not provide enough evidence to judge the clinical drug interactions of curcumin
citations.label: Bahramsoltani et al., 2017, J Ethnopharmacol
citations.title: Pharmacokinetic interactions of curcuminoids with conventional drugs: A review.
